subject.title: fix(doctor): exit non-zero on final invalid config (#77804)

question: Should an invalid final persisted config make plain `openclaw doctor` exit 1, or should non-zero diagnostic gating remain exclusive to `openclaw doctor --lint`?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically implementable, but changing the established plain-command exit contract can break existing wrappers and conflicts with the current documented separation between human doctor and automation lint.

options.title: Keep plain doctor compatible
options.body: Retain the existing plain-doctor exit behavior and direct automation to the already documented `doctor --lint` surface.

options.title: Approve plain fail-closed behavior
options.body: Allow plain doctor to exit 1, but require explicit contract documentation plus fresh-install, upgrade, and wrapper compatibility proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep plain doctor compatible
recommendation.body: Retain the existing plain-doctor exit behavior and direct automation to the already documented `doctor --lint` surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent doctor migration work and broad CLI compatibility ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the product-contract choice.
